result.topic_en: Using the asymptotic behaviour of the harmonic sum up to (3^n-1)/2 to derive a series for Euler's constant gamma, followed by a crossed-out note relating a Mellin-type integral to a power series.
result.transcription:
But when $n$ is very great we know that
$\left(1+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}+\cdots\cdots\frac{1}{\frac{3^n-1}{2}}\right)-n\log 3$
[-$=\gamma+\log$-] $=\gamma-\log 2$ as $n\to\infty$.
Hence $\gamma=\log 2-2\left(\frac{1}{3^3-3}\right)[-+-]-4\left(\frac{1}{6^3-6}+\frac{1}{9^3-9}+\frac{1}{12^3-12}\right)^{3}$[?]
[-$\int_0^\infty x^{n-1}F(x)\,dx=\Gamma(n)\,\mu_{-n}$-]
[-then $F(x)=\mu_0-\frac{x}{\lfloor 1}\mu_1+\frac{x^2}{\lfloor 2}\mu_2-\cdots$-]

methods.what: Asymptotic of the harmonic sum up to (3^n-1)/2 minus n log 3 tends to gamma - log 2
Series expression for Euler's constant gamma in terms of log 2 and sums of 1/(k^3-k) over multiples of 3
(Crossed out) Mellin transform relation and corresponding power series expansion of F (Ramanujan's master theorem form)

items.english: But when n is very large we know that (the harmonic sum up to (3^n-1)/2 minus n log 3 tends to gamma - log 2).
If the integral from 0 to infinity of x^(n-1)F(x) dx equals Gamma(n) mu_{-n}, then F(x) = mu_0 - x/1! mu_1 + x^2/2! mu_2 - ... (crossed out).
